sections.title: African Power and Atlantic Empires, 1600-1900
sections.description: This seminar examines the relationship between African political authority and Atlantic empires between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries. Connecting West Central Africa (the Kingdom of Kongo and Angola), the Gold Coast, and the Bight of Benin to Brazil, Cuba, Jamaica, and Haiti, the course explores how slavery, abolition, revolution, and imperial expansion reshaped political life across the Atlantic world. Through historical and interdisciplinary scholarship, students will analyze sovereignty, violence, diplomacy, and ritual authority while examining how African and Afro-diasporic actors shaped the making of the modern Atlantic world.
